rationale:
structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery` are the `#[non_exhaustive]` struct `TextQuery` with public fields `scope: SourceScope`, `pattern: String`, `context_lines: usize` and `limit: Option<usize>`. They also include the constructor and builder signatures `new(String)`, `scope(self, SourceScope)`, `context_lines(self, usize)` and `limit(self, usize)`, each returning `Self`. All of these are in the roots and match.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#struct[TextQuery]` has the attribute and the four fields with the prescribed types.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[new]` takes `pattern: String`. It sets `scope` to `SourceScope::all()`, `context_lines` to 0 and `limit` to `None`. `SourceScope::all()` is documented as selecting all visible project files.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[scope]` and `impl[TextQuery]/fn[context_lines]` take `self` by value, set their field and return `self`.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[limit]` takes `usize`, sets `Some(limit)` and returns `self`.

The other clauses describe observable search behavior, so I treated them as discretionary and left them to the tests. These are: `pattern` is a regular expression, `context_lines` returns that many lines on either side of a match, and `limit` bounds matches across the scope. The text names no regex library and no interface to delegate to. A different engine or traversal would give the same results. So these clauses create no structural obligation needing implementation evidence.

behavioral: The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery`.

- **Defaults:** `TextQuery::new` is asserted to have `limit == None` and `context_lines == 0`. Searching with it over two files returns all three matches across both files, with `complete` true. That shows the default scope covers every file and that `None` means all matches. With zero context, each excerpt is just the matching line (`starts_with("hit")` and a length of four).
- **`scope` override:** `scope(SourceScope::under("one.txt"))` restricts the results to the one file. The entries are asserted by path, line and excerpt, and the other file's hit is absent.
- **`context_lines` override:** The test asserts exact excerpts.
  - With one line of context, a middle match gives the line before, the match and the line after.
  - With two lines, it gives the whole five-line file.
  - The first match in the scoped file has no line before it, and the last match has no line after it. Both excerpts are truncated at the file edge as expected.
- **`limit` override and bounding across the scope:** `limit(2)` over the unscoped, two-file search returns two matches with `complete` false. A per-file limit would return three, so this shows the limit applies across the scope. `limit(1)` on the scoped query returns one match with `complete` false.
- **`pattern` as a regular expression:** The pattern `^hit[0-9]$` uses an anchor and a character class, and the results match them.

The other marked test, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, only checks the public export inventory. It adds nothing to the behavioral obligations here.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.

text: `TextQuery::new(pattern)` searches all visible files, with zero context lines and
no match limit. `scope`, `context_lines`, and `limit` override those defaults.

`pattern` is a regular expression. `context_lines` requests that many lines on either side of each matching line. Zero returns just the matching line. `limit` bounds matches across the scope. `None` requests all matches.
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn context_lines(self, context_lines: usize) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
